audit_findings.title: Known 2026 customer loss is absent from the earnings perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $1.8 million of 2025 gross profit, equal to 11.0% of the $16.4 million anchor; attributable after-tax OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Known contract expiration reduces normalized post-March 2026 OE, but the null perimeter and nondeclining scenarios retain historical earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We have been informed by one of our significant operations and maintenance customers that it will not extend its existing contract with PERC beyond its expiration date in March 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated omission, not merely a possibility. The contract expired in 2026, and the latest filing reports lower O&M revenue following two customer expirations. The disclosed gross profit is large relative to the anchor and therefore reasonably capable of materially reducing operating value.
audit_findings.action: Remove the lost contract's attributable after-tax OE from the anchor and all forecast years, add back only documented replacement earnings, and rerun every scenario and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Retail-license economics may be structurally worse than the historical anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: filed pro forma operating-income reduction of $1.9 million for 2025, equal to 11.6% of the anchor; computed all-else-equal base-value reduction of approximately $26.8 million or $1.66 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The new license reduces normalized retail operating income and OE relative to the historical rate structure capitalized by the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: We have been informed during our retail license negotiations, both by OfReg and its predecessor in these negotiations, that they seek to restructure the terms of the license in a manner that could significantly reduce the operating income and cash flows we have historically generated from our retail license.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves the earlier uncertainty: a 25-year license became effective August 1, 2026, and management estimates that its terms would have reduced 2025 operating income by $1.9 million. Because the valuation date follows the license issuance but the perimeter is null, the historical anchor demonstrably overstates post-license economics.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild normalized retail OE using the filed new-license rates, energy mechanism, meter fees and pro forma reductions; then rerun the OE anchor, scenarios and buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: A material bulk contract had expired by the valuation date
audit_findings.magnitude: filed first-half 2026 revenue of $1,410,624 from the two agreements, equal to 2.2% of consolidated first-half revenue; attributable OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrenewal after the current extension would reduce future bulk OE and could make long-horizon growth assumptions too high.
audit_findings.evidence: Our agreement with the WAC for the North Sound and NSWW plants expires on July 1, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The specific claimed expiration was not present at the valuation date: the latest filing states that both agreements were extended through March 31, 2027. Continuity after that date remains a forward-looking renewal risk, but the supplied record does not demonstrate a current earnings omission or establish the contracts' attributable profit.
audit_findings.action: Monitor for a renewal or replacement before March 31, 2027; if continuity is not contractually secured, remove the agreements' attributable OE from post-expiry forecast years and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Persistent delinquent receivables may make accounting OE exceed distributable cash
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $18.8 million WSC receivable at June 30, 2026, of which 64% or a computed $12.0 million was delinquent; expected-loss and recurring working-capital effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A credit loss would reduce OE or equity value, while permanently slow collections would require a normalized working-capital charge against distributable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of February 28, 2026, this receivable amounted to $22.6 million, of which 75% was delinquent.
audit_findings.explanation: The receivable and collection delay are demonstrated, but a valuation error is not yet established. The balance declined from $22.6 million in February to $18.8 million in June, delinquency improved from 75% to 64%, and prior delinquent balances were ultimately collected. The record does not show whether the OE calculation already captures normalized working-capital investment or what loss, if any, should be recognized.
audit_findings.action: Obtain subsequent collection records and aging, calculate historical WSC cash-conversion and delinquency levels, confirm the OE working-capital treatment, and rerun with evidence-based expected-loss and normalized working-capital charges.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer funding committed to future performance
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $12.407 million of contract liabilities, equal to 9.4% of $132.629 million cash; a conservative full bridge deduction would reduce base value by $0.77 per share or 3.4%
audit_findings.mechanism: Any customer-funded cash required to satisfy remaining performance obligations is not surplus cash and should be excluded from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Contract liabilities, which include billings in excess of costs and estimated earnings on uncompleted contracts, represent the Company's obligation to transfer goods or services to a customer for which the Company has been paid by the customer or for which the Company has billed the customer under the terms of the contract.
audit_findings.explanation: Contract liabilities confirm customer billings or payments ahead of performance, but they do not establish that an equal amount of cash remains restricted or that future fulfillment costs are absent from projected OE. Even deducting the entire filed liability as a conservative proxy would leave the base value well below the $29.28 market price and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile contract liabilities to cash receipts, remaining contract costs and restrictions; rerun the bridge only for the amount demonstrated to be unavailable to owners, together with separately established minimum operating cash.

audit_findings.title: Parent-level OE is paired with consolidated cash partly attributable to minority owners
audit_findings.magnitude: computed minority claim of approximately $1.71 million on the filed $18.8 million Bahamas cash balance at 9.1%, equal to about $0.11 per share and 0.47% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge assigns consolidated subsidiary cash wholly to CWCO shareholders although parent-attributable OE excludes the minority share of subsidiary earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We own 90.9% of CW-Bahamas, which provides bulk water under long-term contracts to the Water and Sewerage Corporation of The Bahamas (“WSC”), a government agency.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, but its identifiable scale is not material to the conclusion. Assuming all filed Bahamas cash belongs to 90.9%-owned CW-Bahamas, correcting the minority claim reduces value by only about $0.11 per share and leaves every scenario below the market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm entity-level cash ownership and deduct 9.1% of CW-Bahamas cash, plus any minority claim on other bridge assets, in the next bridge rerun.
